The election of the member of a confirmed right-wing extremist, anti-constitutional party as house speaker meant that a "border" had been crossed, she said. "We will not allow ourselves to be intimidated, and we will not sit by when rights here or those of the people in this state are to be curtailed," she added. Earlier in her address, she said that if the AfD were to take power in the state, her party would "speak out if people were denigrated because of their origins, beliefs or lifestyle." Sziborra-Seidlitz said Saxony-Anhalt could not afford for "exclusion to become the political brand of this parliament and our state." The AfD emerged from September elections as the strongest single force in parliament but has so far failed to find parties willing to enter into a coalition with it. The Saxony-Anhalt chapter of the party has been classified as "confirmed right-wing extremist" by the domestic intelligence agency in the state. Among other things, the party advocates a hard-line anti-immigration agenda and an intolerant stance toward LGBTQ+ rights. https://p.dw.com/p/5NqEO Skip next section Far-right AfD candidate elected state parliamentary speaker 10/06/2026 October 6, 2026 Far-right AfD candidate elected state parliamentary speaker Timothy Jones Tobias Rausch has been in the Saxony-Anhalt parliament since 2016 Image: dts-Agentur/picture alliance Tobias Rausch, the far-right Alternative for Germany 's (AFD's) nomination for speaker in Saxony-Anhalt 's state parliament, has been elected with the help of the populist BSW party. Rausch gained 48 votes in favor to 29 against from 82 eligible votes. There were five abstentions. The AfD holds 39 seats in the parliament and the BSW five, giving Rausch the majority he needed to win the post, as the other parties combined — all of which reject working with the AfD — also hold 39 seats. The result, however, means that members of parties besides the AfD and BSW voted for him. Rausch, 35, thus becomes the first member of the AfD — a party classified by domestic intelligence in Saxony-Anhalt as a "confirmed right-wing extremist" organization — to become speaker in a state parliament in Germany. The new speaker is a real-estate entrepreneur by profession and has been a member of parliament for the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt since 2016. The parliamentary session was accompanied by several anti-AfD protests in front of the parliament building. The vote for speaker is separate from that for state premier. The AfD's lead candidate, Ulrich Siegmund, who won the September election with 44% of the vote — thus falling short of an absolute majority — intends to stand for the position in December. As no other party so far wants to form a coalition with his party, it is still in question whether he can win a vote or form a government. "I am aware that balancing all of these constraints is not easy. I am also aware of the difficult budgetary situation in the member states," von der Leyen told the European Parliament in the French city of Strasbourg. "But I would like to caution against large cuts. They would risk undermining critical priorities that we have all agreed upon," she added. Negotiations on the long-term budget for the 2028-2034 period are currently underway. The EU's long-term budget , also known as the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), is the European Union's seven-year spending plan that sets how much the bloc can spend and on which priorities, such as agriculture , regional development, research, defense , migration , and climate policy . The European Commission has proposed a budget of around €1.76 trillion (about $1.98 trillion). The budget is financed mainly through contributions based on the size of member states' economies. The current MFF for 2021-2027 amounts to around €1.2 trillion. Traditionally, Germany has opposed increases to the proposed budget, while other countries favor maintaining subsidies for economically disadvantaged regions. This time has been no different, with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz calling for major cuts. Ireland , which currently holds the rotating EU presidency, is expected to present a new compromise proposal in the coming days. The sharp increase comes after Germany's new military service law came into effect on January 1. That law foresees mandatory medical screening for young men born in 2008 or later, with an eye to recruiting volunteers to expand the armed forces. Although compulsory military service has been suspended in Germany since 2011, it remains enshrined in Germany's Basic Law. The right to refuse armed military service as a conscientious objector also remains in place. The AfD holds 39 seats in the legislature, the same number of seats as the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) , the Left Party , Greens and Social Democrats (SPD) together. During the session, parliamentarians are to vote for a speaker, with the AfD, as the strongest force, empowered to nominate the first candidate. The AfD has put forward long-serving parliamentarian Tobias Rausch, 35, for the post, a choice that the populist BSW, which holds 5 seats, has pledged to back. All the other parties refuse to work with the AfD under a policy known as the "firewall," and the CDU chairman in the state has advised members of his party to abstain from the vote. If Rausch is elected, he will become the first AfD speaker of a state parliament in Germany. However, if he fails to be elected in a first round of voting, all the other parties can put forward their own candidates. There will be no vote on who will lead the state. Trending POLAND TOWNSHIP – Indian Trail resident Don Kromer is seeking assistance in dealing with a severe flooding situation on his property and is asking the Poland Forest Board to clear out a drain and remove dead wood from the forest. The issue for Kromer is not a new one. It has been an issue for the past three years. Anytime there is a hard rain in a short time, his property floods. "I have had 7 feet of water in my back yard," Kromer said. "I own two acres, but when it rains, I am down to one acre that I can enjoy." Kromer's property is in Poland Township and is bordered by Boardman Township and the Poland Forest and Poland Village. His property is at the low spot for drainage of surrounding neighborhoods. The rear of Kromer's property was actually where an original county sanitary lift pump station was located. He said more than four years ago, the county sanitary district moved the lift station from the back of his property to the front side that borders Boardman. He said in exchange, he received the back section of property, including a raised area that contains the sanitary sewer line. The big issue for Kromer is the creek that cuts across the Boardman side of his property and flows through a culvert into Poland Forest. The creek then winds down to Yellow Creek through a second culvert. This year alone, Kromer said his property has flooded multiple times. Any storm with 1 inch or more of rain in a short time causes severe flooding in his rear yard. He has one area where he parks his fishing boat on a trailer. The most recent flood almost floated the boat while it was still attached. "In the past three years, I have been to meetings in Boardman Township, Poland Township, Poland Village, the Mahoning County Commissioners, and the Poland Forest Board," he said. "On Sept. 28, 2026, I went to the Forest Board meeting and put them on notice for fallen trees and clogged drainage." Kromer said he wants three things done. One is to clear the culvert that runs from his property into the park. The second is to clear the fallen trees from the creek that flows from the culvert. Finally, he wants the dead wood removed from around his property. Mark Thompson from the Poland Forest Board walked the area in question and checked out Kromer’s claims. The culvert Kromer said is clogged was photographed by Thompson. "The park end of the culvert is not clogged," Thompson said. As for the creek being clogged with limbs, Thompson said there are fallen trees lying in and across the creek. "It does not have a significant impact on the flow," Thompson said. The Forest Board does not remove the dead wood from the forest, preferring to keep it natural. Many trees were ash and were killed by the emerald ash borer over the past decade. Kromer insists the culvert needs to be cleaned out and the dead wood removed from around the creek. He plans to keep on striving for that solution, which he believes will ease the flooding issues. "All I want to do is enjoy my property," he said. "All of it." Starting at /week. Subscribe Today
